nodes.name: NiFeMo Electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Prior to electrodeposition, the commercial nickel foam (1×3 cm²) was removed residual organic species and oxides on the surface via our previous method [19]. In a typical synthesis, a piece of nickel foam (1×3 cm²) and two parallel-arranged graphite rods were used as the cathode and anode electrode, respectively. As shown in Scheme. 1, the electrodeposition was conducted in a home-made two-electrode system at room temperature. Constant current deposition was carried out at -300 mA for 15 min at room temperature. The electrolyte for preparing NiFeMo hybrid film was an aqueous solution containing 0.17 M Ni(NO3)2, 0.13 M FeSO4, 0.12 M Na2MoO4, and 0.27 M C6H5Na3O7 by dissolving each chemical in 50 mL deionized water.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows NiFeMo films with thickness of 500 nm attached on Ni foam substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In SEM observation (Fig. S1a in the Supporting Information), the as-deposited NiFeMo films with the thickness of 500 nm are attached on Ni Foam substrate.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM-EDS maps confirm Ni, Fe, and Mo elements homogeneously distributed throughout the NiFeMo films.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM-EDS maps of (Fig. S1b) confirm that the main elements of Ni, Fe and Mo homogeneously distribute throughout the entire films.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows broad peak at 40°-50° for poorly crystalline metal Ni, peaks at 11.5°, 23.1°, 35.0° for (003), (006), (009) planes of 2Ni(OH)₂-NiOOH with slight shift to high angle indicating Fe incorporation, no detectable Mo-containing or Fe phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The main broad diffraction peak at 40° - 50° of XRD patterns of NiFeMo sample (Fig. 1a) can be indexed to metal Ni with poor crystallinity ... no significant diffraction peaks of the Mo-containing phases can be detected.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ni 2p shows Ni⁰ (852.11 eV), Ni²⁺ (855.43/873.06 eV), Ni³⁺ (856.33/874.16 eV); Fe 2p shows Fe⁰ (705.50 eV), Fe²⁺ (710.62/724.06 eV), Fe³⁺ (712.57/726.60 eV); Mo 3d shows MoOₓ (235.50/252.35 eV); O 1s shows M-O(OH) (529.9 eV), defective oxide (530.9 eV), MoOₓ (531.70 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1b, the high-resolution spectra of Ni 2p can be divided into two spin-orbit doublets. The two-doublet binding energies at 855.43 and 873.06 eV and at 856.33 and 874.16 eV correspond to Ni²⁺ and Ni³⁺ ... Mo 3d spectrum (Fig. 1d) can be fitted into two spit-orbit peaks of Mo 3d3/2 at 252.35 eV and Mo 3d5/2 at 235.50 eV ... The fitting peaks of O 1s (Fig. S3) show three peaks at 529.9 eV corresponding to M-O(OH), 530.9 eV corresponding to defective oxide, and 531.70 eV corresponding to MoOₓ.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes of 0.73 nm for (003) plane of 2Ni(OH)₂-NiOOH (less than standard 0.77 nm), lattice distortions, and abundant amorphous sections.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image of NiFeMo (Fig. 2a) displays lattice fringes with the interplanar distances of 0.73 nm ... Notably, Fig. 2c presents that ample lattice distortions exist in crystal lattices and abundant amorphous section can be observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals abundant nanoporous structure with maximum pore size of 40 nm, exposing low-coordinated steps, edges, and dangling bonds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, abundant "nanoporous" with maximum pore size of 40 nm can be observed in transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images of NiFeMo (Fig. 2d,e).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows peaks at ~310 cm⁻¹ (FeOOH), 495 cm⁻¹ (disordered Ni(OH)₂), 683 cm⁻¹ (NiO), 893 cm⁻¹ (Mo-O), 470/550 cm⁻¹ (NiOOH type phase).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra of initial NiFeMo in Fig. 6f show some peaks at ∼310 cm⁻¹, 495 cm⁻¹, 683 cm⁻¹ and 893 cm⁻¹, which is corresponding to the vibration peaks of FeOOH ... the e_g bending and the A_{1g} stretching vibration of Ni-O in the NiOOH type phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of NiFe indexed to nickel oxide hydroxide with poor crystallinity; NiMo shows metal Ni phase; FeMo shows no crystalline phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For comparison, the XRD patterns (Fig. S2) of NiFe, NiMo and FeMo were also given. The XRD pattern of NiFe (Fig. S2a) is indexed to Nickel oxide hydroxide with poor crystallinity. The XRD pattern of NiMo (Fig. S2b) exhibits the metal Ni phase. There is no crystalline phase in the XRD pattern of FeMo (Fig. S2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS of NiFe shows shift in Fe 2p to lower binding energy after Mo incorporation, indicating increased low-valence Fe²⁺; Ni 2p and O 1s shift to higher binding energy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS measurements of NiFe are performed to further investigate the possible electric interaction between the NiFe and the Mo species. After the incorporation of Mo, an apparently shift towards lower binding energy was observed in Fe 2p of NiFeMo as shown in Fig. S4b ... Meanwhile, the peaks of Ni 2p (Fig. S4a) and O 1s (Fig. S4c) in NiFeMo shifted to marginally higher binding energy.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV used to calculate electrochemical double-layer capacitance Cdl values: NiFeMo 7.9 mF cm⁻², NiFe 5.0 mF cm⁻², NiMo 5.1 mF cm⁻², FeMo 3.4 mF cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical surface area (ECSA) of different electrocatalysts was measured by cyclic voltammetry technique ... Cdl values of those catalysts calculated from CV plots (Fig. S7) are presented in Fig. 4d. The NiFeMo sample has a value of 7.9 mF cm⁻², higher than those of NiFe (5.0 mF cm⁻²), NiMo (5.1 mF cm⁻²), FeMo (3.4 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV and Laviron's method used to calculate redox constants ks for OH⁻ adsorption: NiFe 0.21 s⁻¹, NiFeMo 0.19 s⁻¹, NiMo 0.16 s⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, the adsorption for OH⁻ of NiFeMo, NiFe and NiMo was investigated by cyclic voltammetry (CV) and Laviron's method (Fig. S6, see details in Supporting Information). The calculated value of redox constants (ks) means the adsorption strength for OH⁻ in redox reaction.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS Nyquist plots show NiFeMo has lowest charge-transfer resistance Rct among all samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Coincident with the HER activity, the Nyquist plots (Fig. 3c) and the fitting parameters (Fig. S5) from the equivalent circuit (inset of Fig. S5) indicate that the NiFeMo electrode delivers the lowest charge-transfer resistance (R_ct) value among all samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman of NiFe shows peak at 523 cm⁻¹ assigned to Ni-O.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the initial NiFe sample, the peak at 523 cm⁻¹ is assigned to Ni-O.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER/UOR XPS of NiFeMo shows Ni 2p, Mo 3d, O 1s red-shift to lower binding energy; Fe 2p up-shift with increased Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺ ratio from 0.804 to 0.915; disappearance of Ni⁰ and Fe⁰ signals; increased O2 peak strength indicating (oxy)hydroxide formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The main peaks of Ni 2p, Mo 3d and O 1s red-shift to lower binding energy after OER and UOR, as shown in Fig. 6. ... The Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺ ratio calculated by integrating peak areas is increased from 0.804 to 0.915 ... The peak strength of O2 (oxygen in metal hydroxyl group) in O 1s region increases significantly.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER/UOR TEM shows typical nanosheets structure and 0.25 nm lattice fringe for (012) planes of NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, using TEM and HRTEM study, we further observed the phase transformation of NiFeMo after OER and UOR. As shown in Fig. S9a, the lattice fringe with a 0.25 nm distance can be assigned to the (012) lattice planes of NiFe LDH ... The typical nanosheets structure observed in TEM image (Fig. S9b) further demonstrate the existence of NiFe LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-long-term stability SEM shows no obvious change in NiFeMo surface structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the long-term stability test, no obvious change was observed in the surface structure of the NiFeMo electrode (inset SEM images of Fig. S11a).

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-long-term UOR EDS shows significantly increased O content on anode electrode surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS spectrum (Fig. S11b and S11c) demonstrate that the content of O element on the surface of anode electrode increased significantly after long-term UOR.
